verses.1: Praise the LORD. Sing to the LORD a new song; praise His praise in the assembly of the faithful.
verses.2: Let Israel rejoice in its Maker; let the sons of Zion be glad in their King.
verses.3: Let them praise His name in dance; with tambourine and lyre, let them sing to Him.
verses.4: For the LORD delights in His people; He exalts the humble in salvation.
verses.5: Let the faithful rejoice in glory; let them sing for joy on their beds.
verses.6: Let the praises of God be in their throats; let two-edged swords be in their hands.
verses.7: To carry out judgment on the nations, to execute reproofs among the peoples.
verses.8: To bind their kings with chains, their nobles with fetters of iron.
verses.9: To carry out on them a judgment written; this is the glory for all His faithful ones. Praise the LORD!

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: The term הַלְלוּ יָהּ is a poetic contraction of הַלְלוּ יָהּ (Praise the LORD). The phrase שִׁיר חָדָשׁ (a new song) is standard in praise psalms.
- v. 6: "two-edged swords" (פִּיפִיּוֹת) is a poetic term for weapons of war, rendered clearly based on contextual and semantic understanding.

[3] Let them praise His name in dance; with tambourine and lyre, let them sing to Him.

[6] Let the praises of God be in their throats; let two-edged swords be in their hands.

[7] To carry out judgment on the nations, to execute reproofs among the peoples.

[8] To bind their kings with chains, their nobles with fetters of iron.

[9] To carry out on them a judgment written; this is the glory for all His faithful ones. Praise the LORD!
